title: Mill jobs table and source sheet
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Victorian Britain and the Industrial Revolution (Revolution)
source: Written for history/y6 lesson 17 (Mill jobs table and source sheet (portal printable; teacher-written summaries of 1830s evidence))
intro: Lesson 17: Working lives in mills and factories. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Summary of a factory inspector's report
panels.text: Children in many mills worked about 12 hours a day. Many were tired; some had injuries from machines. The report was written to give Parliament evidence for new laws limiting children's hours.

model.title: What does the report summary tell us?

parts.text: Fact: they were tired and some were injured
Who: people collecting evidence for new laws
Use: good evidence, written to show problems

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Useful evidence of hard conditions, collected to argue for change

keywords.def: what it is like to be somewhere
children doing paid work instead of school
a person who watched and controlled workers

questions.q: How long was a typical mill shift?
Give one danger in a mill.
questions.a: Moving machines, dust, long hours, tiredness

questions.q: Core: Write a diary of a day in a mill as a child worker, using five facts from today. Write in the portal response box, starting 'At half past five the bell rang...'
questions.a: A diary with at least five accurate facts about hours, jobs, dangers and pay

questions.q: Extend: Compare a mill child's day with your school day (three differences).
Stretch: Why might a mill owner say children were happy?
questions.a: To avoid new laws and keep costs low
A) They were paid less. Mill owners paid children less, and families needed the money.

questions.q: Big question: should children work full time?
questions.a: No: they need education, rest and safety, as later laws agreed
